holidays.name: National Pop Goes the Weasel Day
holidays.description: Break out your best sing-song voice and belt out the nursery rhyme that ends with a sudden jack-in-the-box surprise. Bonus points for popping up unexpectedly on the final line.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and nobody knows who started it. It celebrates a nursery rhyme and dance tune that children have sung for hundreds of years.
holidays.funFact: The tune was a huge dance craze in 1850s England and America. The 'weasel' may be Cockney rhyming slang for something pawned, though historians still debate what the lyrics really mean.

holidays.name: International Bath Day
holidays.description: This is an official excuse to fill the tub, add bubbles, and soak. Bring a rubber duck, a book, and a very good reason not to answer your phone.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It nods to the legend of Archimedes and his 'Eureka!' bath-time discovery.
holidays.funFact: According to legend, Archimedes was so excited by his bathtub discovery about water displacement that he ran through the streets without any clothes on.

holidays.name: National Bourbon Day
holidays.description: Raise a glass, or a cocktail shaker, to America's native spirit. Sip it neat, stir an Old Fashioned, or cook with it in a barbecue sauce or dessert.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food and drink observance that honors bourbon and the distillers who make it.
holidays.funFact: To be called bourbon, the spirit must be made in the U.S. from at least 51% corn and aged in new charred oak barrels. Most of it is made in Kentucky.
